<explanation>
Below is a step-by-step guide to creating a complete system-design diagram for VERT.sh, tailored to its structure and purpose as a Svelte/TypeScript client-heavy application that does file conversion in the browser and via an optional backend daemon.

1. Identify the project type and purpose  
   • This is primarily a full-stack single-page application (SPA) built with SvelteKit and TypeScript.  
   • It runs entirely in the user’s browser for local (WebAssembly) conversions, but can optionally call an external “vertd” daemon (HTTP API) for non-local, heavier conversions.  
   • Static assets (including WASM modules) are served from a static web server (e.g., Nginx in Docker).  

2. Main architectural components  
   a. Client Browser Layer  
      – SvelteKit UI (src/routes, src/lib/components)  
      – Web Workers (src/lib/workers/*.ts) that load & execute WASM modules (pandoc.wasm, etc.)  
      – Local state management (Svelte stores) and UI logic  
   b. Static Hosting Layer  
      – Vite dev server (bun dev) in development  
      – Built static site → Nginx (Docker container) serving HTML, JS/CSS, WASM, manifest.json  
   c. Optional Backend Service  
      – vertd daemon (external HTTP service) for video conversions  
   d. Third-Party Integrations  
      – Plausible Analytics (via PUB_PLAUSIBLE_URL)  
      – Optional CDN or custom domain (PUB_HOSTNAME)  

3. Key relationships and data flows  
   1. User opens browser → requests HTML/CSS/JS from Nginx (or Vite in dev).  
   2. SvelteKit hydrates UI, user selects a file.  
   3. File is sent to either:  
      • Web Worker → loads appropriate WASM converter (e.g., pandoc.wasm) → returns converted data to UI  
      • OR forwarded via HTTP → vertd backend → streamed back to browser  
   4. UI displays progress via Toasts/ProgressBar components.  
   5. Analytics events are sent to Plausible.  

4. Architectural patterns & design principles  
   • Component-based UI (Svelte components split between functional, layout, visual).  
   • Separation of concerns: UI vs. conversion logic vs. state store vs. workers.  
   • Use of WebWorker pattern to offload CPU-heavy WASM tasks.  
   • Environment-driven configuration (PUB_ENV, PUB_VERTD_URL).  
   • Containerized static hosting (Docker + Nginx) and local dev with Bun.  

5. Technologies & frameworks  
   • Frontend: SvelteKit, TypeScript, Vite, Tailwind, PostCSS, Sass  
   • WASM converters: pandoc.wasm, other wasm modules via Web Workers  
   • Build & runtime: Bun (dev/install), Docker, nginx.conf  
   • State & logging: Svelte stores, custom logger  
   • CI/CD: GitHub Actions (docker.yml)  
   • Linting & formatting: ESLint, Prettier  

6. Tailoring the diagram for this full-stack SPA  
   – Emphasize the client-side conversion path (Web Worker + WASM) vs. server-side via vertd.  
   – Show static asset hosting (Docker→Nginx) separately from dynamic conversion backend.  
   – Highlight environment variables controlling external endpoints.  
   – Represent development flow (Vite dev server) as a side path.  

7. Diagramming guidelines  
   • Use clear, distinct shapes:  
     – Rounded rectangles for services/servers (e.g., “Nginx / Static Host”, “vertd API”)  
     – Rectangles or cylinders for static assets (WASM modules, manifest.json)  
     – Browser icon for the client, with sub-components (UI, Workers) inside  
     – Clouds or external shapes for 3rd-party integrations (Plausible)  
   • Color-code by layer:  
     – Blue for client components  
     – Green for static hosting  
     – Orange for backend/daemon  
     – Gray for external services  
   • Label every component clearly.  
   • Draw directional arrows for requests and data flow:  
     – HTML/CSS/JS fetched → Browser  
     – File payload ➔ Worker/WASM or HTTP ➔ vertd  
     – Analytics ➔ Plausible  
   • Annotate configuration points (e.g., “PUB_VERTD_URL → vertd endpoint”).  

Putting it all together, your final diagram will have the following high-level layout:  
[Client Browser]  
  • UI Components  
  • Svelte Stores  
  • Web Workers ←– WASM Modules  
    ↳ Converts local files  
  • HTTP Module —–> vertd API (optional backend conversion)  
  • Analytics → Plausible  

[Static Hosting (Docker + Nginx)]  
  • Serves built assets (HTML, JS, CSS, WASM)  

[External Services]  
  • vertd conversion daemon  
  • Plausible Analytics  

Ensure your diagram is exhaustive (don’t forget manifest.json, Dockerfile, CI/CD workflow), but also clear by grouping related items. Use a legend for colors/shapes and place arrows to indicate request/response or data flow direction.  
</explanation>
